aspect_assessments.assessment: CVO450 half-cells retain more than 90% of capacity after 600 cycles at 0.2 A g−1 and perform better than CVO550 at elevated current densities (o08, o09, o10).
limitations: Cycle retention reference not stated in the text.
No CVO450 surface-area measurement in the main text (o07 reports CVOp, CVO450 and CVO550 values); SSA is an indirect measure of electrolyte contact.
aspect_assessments.rationale: Direct half-cell observations; the proposed alternative concerns the explanation of this result.
aspect_assessments.scope: CR2032 coin cells with Na metal counter electrodes, 0.01–3 V, room temperature.

aspect_assessments.assessment: Ca2+ remains oxidized during sodiation (o17), and the (110) d-spacing shifts from 0.347 to 0.350 nm on discharge and is recovered on charging (o18).
limitations: Single-cycle ex situ PXRD.
No Ca2+ oxidation-state measurement after repeated cycling.
aspect_assessments.rationale: Direct observations; the structural evidence is limited to ex situ PXRD and HRTEM.
aspect_assessments.scope: CVO450 half-cell electrodes recovered at selected states of the second cycle.

aspect_assessments.assessment: The Ca2+ pillar mechanism is supported by unchanged Ca oxidation state, small (110) d-spacing shift and retained lattice spacing after 600 cycles (o17, o18, o19), but it is not the only factor: CVO450 has a surface area of 19.5 m2 g−1 (o07), and the cited prior report (b05) is for Na-intercalated V2O5 (17% volume expansion).
limitations: No surface-area comparison in the half-cell comparison (e05).
No direct Na expansion measurement in CVO450.
aspect_assessments.rationale: The mechanism is supported by its own evidence, but the surface-area difference is not addressed by it.
aspect_assessments.scope: CVO450 electrode.

findings.description: The half-cell result is explained by the Ca2+ pillar mechanism (n12), but CVO450 has a surface area of 19.5 m2 g−1 (o07) while CVO550 has 33.2 m2 g−1; the cited prior report (b05) is for Na-intercalated V2O5 (17% volume expansion), so the same expansion in CaV8O20 is not established. A surface-area explanation for the half-cell result remains open.
The half-cell comparison (e05) varied only the annealing temperature; surface area was not varied, so the surface-area difference between CVO450 and CVO550 is a factor that was not controlled.
The structural evidence for n06 is limited to ex situ PXRD over the second cycle and HRTEM after 600 cycles; no in situ or in operando measurement is visible.

information_requests: Surface-area values for the electrodes used in the half-cell comparison, or the surface-area difference between the two electrodes, so that the surface-area comparison can be stated quantitatively.

add_nodes.statement: Unverified proposal: CVO450's reversible, stable half-cell cycling (o08, o10) may partly reflect its lower surface area (19.5 m2 g−1, o07) rather than the Ca2+ pillar mechanism, because a higher surface area (33.2 m2 g−1 for CVO550, o07) can expose more Na+ insertion sites but also promote electrolyte decomposition and irreversible Na trapping (i08).

proposed_updates.rationale: The surface-area difference between CVO450 and CVO550 is a factor that was not varied in the half-cell comparison (e05), so it remains an open explanation for the half-cell result. The original Ca2+ pillar mechanism is retained and remains unchallenged by this alternative.

verification_needs.comparison_or_control: CVO450 with surface area 19.5 m2 g−1 (no post-annealing treatment) versus the same electrode after a surface-area-reducing treatment (e.g. annealing at a lower temperature, or a post-annealing treatment that lowers SSA without changing the vanadate framework), with CVO550 as the comparison.
missing_design_information: The surface-area difference between the two electrodes
The surface-area-reducing treatment to apply to CVO450
needed_observations: Specific capacity and capacity retention of CVO450 with the surface-area-reducing treatment over 600 cycles at 0.2 A g−1, and at 0.05 A g−1
verification_needs.unresolved_question: Does reducing CVO450's surface area change its half-cell cycling?
verification_needs.why_informative: If the surface-area-reducing treatment changes the half-cell result, the surface-area explanation is supported; if it does not, the Ca2+ pillar mechanism remains the better explanation.

verification_needs.comparison_or_control: CVO450 versus CVO550 at the same surface area (19.5 m2 g−1 for both) and the same annealing temperature.
needed_observations: Half-cell capacity and retention of CVO450 and CVO550 at 19.5 m2 g−1
verification_needs.unresolved_question: Does the surface-area difference between CVO450 and CVO550 explain the half-cell result?
verification_needs.why_informative: It directly compares the two electrodes while holding surface area constant.

verification_needs.comparison_or_control: Pristine CVO450 and CVO450 with the surface-area-reducing treatment, both tested at 0.2 A g−1.
needed_observations: Ex situ XPS of Ca and V oxidation states after the surface-area-reducing treatment
Ex situ PXRD of the (110) d-spacing after the treatment
verification_needs.unresolved_question: Does the surface-area-reducing treatment change the Ca2+ oxidation state or the lattice spacing?
verification_needs.why_informative: It tests whether the surface-area change affects the structural evidence for the Ca2+ mechanism.

The visible result set shows three things. First, the consortium exceeded the wastewater-only arm by 14.91-fold, exceeded strain SO1 alone by 3.29-fold and strain BS1 alone by 13.34-fold, and reached 50.7 mg/L total. Second, the ethanol-removing partner removed 97.6% of the ethanol within 48 h, which is what the design needs. Third, the later-stage rate fell for every consortium that lacked irrE, from 7.222 to 0.921 mg/L/day for SO1-BS1, from 9.867 to 0.617 mg/L/day for SO2-BS1 and from 10.033 to 1.171 mg/L/day for SO2-BS2, while the irrE-carrying consortium reached 102.4 mg/L total and 3.575 mg/L/day in days 7-14, a 1.47-fold and 3.05-fold increase over its parent. The visible result set therefore already supports the three components of the map, and the next test is whether the consortium can be run at the higher loadings and on different days of the same production run. The map already contains the node n04, which is what the extended campaign needs to test. So the correct action is to request the new measurements and to preserve the existing map.

The map has two problems. First, n12 combines several aspects and claims a causal chain. The functional data are only a 4-week snapshot of LVEF, GLS, E/e', E/A, LV mass, end-diastolic diameter and infarct size. o06–o11 show that transplantation ameliorates these outcomes in MI rats, but they do not establish whether the effects are sustained or whether they persist in the absence of the transplant. The histology and protein data show that myocardial hypertrophy, fibrosis and profibrotic markers are reduced, but they do not establish that the transplant prevents heart failure. The DHE data show lower superoxide in the transplanted MI group, but they do not establish that this is the mechanism by which the other outcomes are improved. The inflammatory and ER stress data are parallel changes. The conclusion also combines effects in MI rats with effects in non-infarcted rats, where no differences were found. So the claim should be rewritten as a statement of the observed association at 4 weeks, with the causal and sustained links removed. Second, n05 is stated as a decrease in superoxide, but o14 shows that superoxide was not increased with transplantation, and o15 shows no change in SOD1 or SOD2 mRNA. The wording should be changed to reflect that superoxide was unchanged. The rest of the map is correct: the aspects cover the different endpoints, the composition edges connect the aspects to the overall aim, and the evidence edges connect each aspect to its observations. The verification needs include a longer follow-up and a mechanistic test.

aspect_assessments.assessment: The claim bundles several associations observed at 4 weeks after MI: preserved LV function and reduced LV mass and fibrosis in MI rats, and lower superoxide, lower inflammation and lower ER stress activation. It does not state that the functional benefits are sustained beyond 4 weeks, that the transplant prevents heart failure, or that the superoxide decrease is the mechanism.
limitations: No sustained follow-up
No mechanistic test linking superoxide to the functional outcomes
No comparison of the two groups without transplantation at later times
The DHE region is not specified
aspect_assessments.rationale: The observations are linked to n12 through ed15–ed19, and they address the bundled aspects of function, remodeling, superoxide, inflammation and ER stress.
aspect_assessments.scope: Male Wistar rats, 4 weeks after MI; Sham + PBS, Sham + mitochondria, MI + PBS and MI + mitochondria; the functional endpoints include LVEF, GLS, E/e', E/A, LV mass, end-diastolic diameter and infarct size.

aspect_assessments.assessment: The functional aspects are supported: LVEF and GLS are preserved, E/e' is improved and LV mass and end-diastolic diameter are lower in MI + mitochondria rats at 4 weeks.
limitations: Functional indices are measured once at the end of the 4-week period
aspect_assessments.rationale: o06, o07 and o09 are linked to n03, and their comparators are MI vs Sham with transplantation.
aspect_assessments.scope: End-diastolic diameter and infarct size in the final week of the 4-week period.

aspect_assessments.assessment: The remodeling aspects are supported: cardiomyocyte CSA and interstitial collagen volume fraction are lower, and collagen I and CCN2 protein are lower in MI + mitochondria rats at 4 weeks.
limitations: The DHE region is not specified
aspect_assessments.rationale: o10, o11 and o12 are linked to n04.
aspect_assessments.scope: 4 weeks after MI; histology on 4 μm paraffin sections and Western blot.

aspect_assessments.assessment: The superoxide aspect is not supported as a decrease. o14 shows that superoxide was not increased with transplantation, and o15 shows no change in SOD1 or SOD2 mRNA.
limitations: No decrease in superoxide is reported
aspect_assessments.rationale: n05 is linked to o14 and o15, but those observations do not show a decrease.
aspect_assessments.scope: Cardiac DHE fluorescence density and SOD1/SOD2 mRNA at 4 weeks.

aspect_assessments.assessment: The inflammatory marker aspect is supported: CCL2 and TLR4 mRNA are lower in MI + mitochondria rats at 4 weeks.
aspect_assessments.rationale: o16 is linked to n06.
aspect_assessments.scope: Cardiac CCL2 and TLR4 mRNA at 4 weeks.

aspect_assessments.assessment: The ER stress aspect is supported: BiP, CHOP, ATF4 and ATF6α protein are lower in MI + mitochondria rats at 4 weeks.
aspect_assessments.rationale: o18 and o19 are linked to n07.
aspect_assessments.scope: Cardiac ER stress proteins at 4 weeks.

aspect_assessments.assessment: The claim that no differences were found in non-infarcted rats covers all parameters evaluated, including the cardiac and renal endpoints, and is supported by o34.
aspect_assessments.rationale: o34 is linked to n01.
aspect_assessments.scope: Sham + PBS vehicle vs Sham + mitochondria at 4 weeks; non-infarcted rats.

findings.description: n12 combines several associations observed at 4 weeks after MI into one statement and claims a causal chain that is not established: preserved LV function and reduced LV mass and fibrosis are reported in MI + mitochondria rats, but the claim does not state that the functional benefits are sustained beyond 4 weeks, that the transplant prevents heart failure, or that the superoxide decrease is the mechanism by which the other outcomes are improved. It also combines effects in MI rats with effects in non-infarcted rats, where no differences were found.
n05 states that mitochondrial transplantation lowers cardiac superoxide levels, but o14 shows that superoxide was not increased with transplantation and o15 shows no change in SOD1 or SOD2 mRNA.

replace_nodes.statement: In MI rats, mitochondrial transplantation was associated with preserved LV function, reduced LV mass and fibrosis, and lower cardiac superoxide, inflammation and ER stress activation at 4 weeks after MI; the functional benefits were observed in the absence of differences in infarct size. No differences were found in non-infarcted rats in any of the parameters evaluated. These associations do not establish sustained effects beyond 4 weeks, prevention of heart failure or a causal chain in which the superoxide decrease mediates the other improvements.

proposed_updates.rationale: The revised wording of n12 states the observed associations at 4 weeks, the absence of differences in non-infarcted rats, and the limits of the causal and sustained links. It removes the causal chain and the sustained effects claim.

replace_nodes.statement: In MI rats, cardiac superoxide was not increased with mitochondrial transplantation at 4 weeks; SOD1 and SOD2 mRNA were unchanged in all groups.

proposed_updates.rationale: The revised wording of n05 reflects the observations o14 and o15, which show that superoxide was not increased with transplantation and that SOD1 and SOD2 mRNA were unchanged.

verification_needs.comparison_or_control: MI + mitochondria vs MI + PBS vehicle at matched time points; sham groups as reference
needed_observations: LV function and LV mass at later times, for example 8 or 12 weeks after MI
verification_needs.unresolved_question: Are the functional benefits sustained beyond 4 weeks?
verification_needs.why_informative: It would test the sustained effects component of the claim rather than treating the 4-week snapshot as a permanent treatment effect.

verification_needs.comparison_or_control: MI + mitochondria vs MI + PBS vehicle with a mitochondrial-depletion or superoxide-raising intervention
needed_observations: LV function and LV mass after an intervention that changes superoxide levels, with mitochondrial transplantation
Superoxide, SOD1 and SOD2 mRNA as readouts
verification_needs.unresolved_question: Is the superoxide decrease responsible for the functional improvements?
verification_needs.why_informative: It would test the causal chain between superoxide and the functional outcomes rather than assuming it from co-occurrence.

<think>
n05 says electrons reach solid NCM through MtrC and OmcA and through riboflavin as shuttle. o28 and o29 show S. oneidensis on the NCM surface for the three consortia, and o02 shows the S. oneidensis arm raising total leaching from 3.4 to 15.4 mg/L, which is exactly the part that needs the electron route. o30 and o31 show the deletion series: the mtrC and omcA deletions lower power density by 9.5-15.9 times and lower total leaching by 6.13-7.64 times, while the double deletion gives 13.4 mg/L, the same as BS3 alone. So the MtrC/OmcA route is the part of the electron transfer that depends on S. oneidensis and on the consortia. The riboflavin part comes from o32: reduced riboflavin oxidises in the same suspension, and the only change between o32 and o28 is that o32 is cell-free. That is what the cell-free aspect n17 is for, and it is a different observation from the consortium-level read-outs. The two routes are therefore not alternatives, they are two parts of the same electron-transfer question, and they are supported by different evidence. n14 merges them and should be split into the two statements. The preserved part is the leaching arm of the deletion series, which shows that the two deletions lower total leaching, which is what the claim says. The verification need is to measure the same thing without the S. oneidensis partner, so that the MtrC/OmcA route is separated from the effect of the partner itself.
</think>

aspect_assessments.assessment: Supported for the MtrC/OmcA route: both deletions lower power density and lower total leaching, and the double-deletion value coincides with BS3 alone, which is the partner alone.
limitations: The deletion strains carry the Ptac::ribADEHC and irrE plasmids, so the deletions are not in wild-type S. oneidensis.
The consortium includes the plasmid-borne strains, so the 13.4 mg/L value is for a two-species system.
aspect_assessments.rationale: o30 and o31 are the deletion series of the claim.
aspect_assessments.scope: Deletion of mtrC, of omcA and of both in the S. oneidensis partner, with the plasmid-borne riboflavin-overproducing and irrE genes, in the SO3-BS3 and deletion consortia, and in strain BS3 alone.

aspect_assessments.assessment: Supported for the riboflavin shuttle: reduced riboflavin oxidises in the same suspension with NCM, and that reaction is cell-free.
limitations: No current or electron-transfer rate is reported for this cell-free reaction.
The observation is a single cell-free reaction at 25 C, while the leaching is at 30 C in brewing wastewater.
aspect_assessments.rationale: o32 is the cell-free observation of the shuttle statement.
aspect_assessments.scope: Cell-free suspension of reduced riboflavin with NCM, 25 C, anoxic, in the dark, for up to 55 min.

aspect_assessments.assessment: Supported as a distinct question: the cell-free riboflavin-NCM reaction is the shuttle part of the electron-transfer route, while the consortium-level read-outs are the MtrC/OmcA route and the presence of S. oneidensis on the NCM surface.
limitations: The cell-free observation is one reaction at one temperature and time course.
aspect_assessments.rationale: n17 is separated from n05 by the cell-free condition, and o32 is the observation for it.
aspect_assessments.scope: Cell-free reaction; not a consortium-level read-out.

aspect_assessments.assessment: Supported for the consortium-level electron-transfer route: S. oneidensis is present on the NCM surface for the three consortia, and the S. oneidensis arm alone raises total leaching from 3.4 to 15.4 mg/L.
limitations: The surface population is relative abundance only; no quantification of the number of cells is given.
The 15.4 mg/L value comes from the S. oneidensis arm alone, and the consortia have B. subtilis as well.
aspect_assessments.rationale: o28 and o29 are the surface read-outs of the consortium-level route, and o02 is the S. oneidensis-only arm.
aspect_assessments.scope: Anaerobic consortium cultures at 30 C for 14 days.

aspect_assessments.assessment: Supported for the reduction mechanism: the XPS fractions show Mn4+ to Mn2+ and Co3+ to Co2+ and Ni3+ to Ni2+ after the consortium treatment.
limitations: The XPS read-out is surface-sensitive and does not give bulk-phase speciation.
aspect_assessments.rationale: o10, o11 and o12 are the XPS observations of the reduction mechanism.
aspect_assessments.scope: Surface-sensitive XPS of the recovered solid after the consortium treatment.

aspect_assessments.assessment: Supported for the leaching question: the consortium raises total leached metal ions from 3.4 to 50.7 mg/L, and the deletions lower total leaching.
limitations: The consortium has two species and the plasmid-borne strains.
No single-species comparison is reported in this packet.
aspect_assessments.rationale: o01-o09 and o31 are the leaching observations.
aspect_assessments.scope: Anaerobic brewing-wastewater cultures at 30 C for 14 days, 0.2 g/L black mass and 1% (v/v) inoculum.

aspect_assessments.assessment: Supported for the shuttle statement: reduced riboflavin oxidises in the same suspension with NCM, and that reaction is cell-free.
limitations: No current or electron-transfer rate is reported for this cell-free reaction.
The observation is a single cell-free reaction at 25 C, while the leaching is at 30 C in brewing wastewater.
aspect_assessments.rationale: o32 is the cell-free observation of the shuttle statement.
aspect_assessments.scope: Cell-free suspension of reduced riboflavin with NCM, 25 C, anoxic, in the dark, for up to 55 min.

findings.description: n14 combines the MtrC/OmcA route with the riboflavin shuttle into one statement, while o30 and o31 support the MtrC/OmcA route by deleting both cytochromes and comparing the values with the partner alone, and o32 supports the shuttle by showing reduced riboflavin oxidising in the same suspension with NCM, a cell-free reaction. The two routes are therefore different parts of the electron-transfer question and need separate statements.

The cell-free riboflavin-NCM reaction (o32) is the shuttle part of the electron-transfer route, while the consortium-level read-outs (o28) are the MtrC/OmcA route and the presence of S. oneidensis on the NCM surface. They are different observations and need separate aspects.

proposed_updates.rationale: The consolidated claim keeps the two routes and the two observations, and the edge from n05 to n14 keeps the claim as a child of the electron-transfer aspect. The verification need is to separate the MtrC/OmcA route from the effect of the S. oneidensis partner.

verification_needs.comparison_or_control: Same conditions without the S. oneidensis partner, with the same plasmid-borne strains and the same riboflavin and irrE genes, so that the MtrC/OmcA route is separated from the partner's contribution.
missing_design_information: Whether the plasmid-borne strains carry any other electron-transfer genes besides the riboflavin-overproduction and irrE genes.
needed_observations: Total leached metal ions from NCM black mass in brewing wastewater without S. oneidensis MR-1, using the plasmid-borne B. subtilis strain carrying the same riboflavin-overproduction and irrE genes as the partner.

verification_needs.why_informative: It separates the contribution of the S. oneidensis partner from the contribution of the MtrC/OmcA route, which is what the current packet cannot do because the deletion strains carry the plasmid-borne partner.

<think>
n13 states that riboflavin molecules captured electrons from S. oneidensis cells through MtrC and OmcA and then reduced NCM. The visible evidence is o30 and o31, which are both read-outs of the SO3 deletion series. o30 shows that the SO3dmtrC-BS3, SO3domcA-BS3 and SO3dmtrCdomcA consortia produced 47.67, 50.01 and 28.39 mW/m2 at most, against 452.90 mW/m2 for the intact SO3-BS3 consortium. o31 shows that those deletion consortia leached 16.7, 18.7 and 13.4 mg/L of total metal ions, against 102.4 mg/L for SO3-BS3. The authors' own interpretation i07 of these results is that MtrC and OmcA were essential for NCM reduction during metal oxide leaching, and o28 shows that the relative abundance of S. oneidensis on the NCM surface rose with the engineering stage of the consortium, from 51.14% for SO1-BS1 to 69.38% for SO3-BS3. No observation in the packet isolates riboflavin from S. oneidensis, and o32 is a cell-free reaction that shows reduced riboflavin passing electrons to NCM. So the wording of n13 claims a step that the visible results cannot show, and the right action is to refine it to the electron-transfer route that the consortium is presumed to use. The alternative electron-transfer route is still a proposed mechanism, and the cell-free riboflavin reaction is kept as a separate aspect.
</think>

limitations: XPS is a surface-sensitive technique.
aspect_assessments.rationale: o10-o12 are the XPS observations of the same SO1-BS1 treatment.
aspect_assessments.scope: Recovered NCM black mass after the SO1-BS1 consortium-catalysed treatment.

aspect_assessments.assessment: The SO1-BS1 consortium leached 50.7 mg/L of total metal ions over 2 weeks, with Li 45.6, Ni 2.4, Co 1.0 and Mn 1.7 mg/L.
aspect_assessments.rationale: o08 is the consortium arm of the four-arm comparison.
aspect_assessments.scope: 0.2 g/L black mass in brewing wastewater at 30 C for 14 days.

aspect_assessments.assessment: MtrC and OmcA were essential: the SO3dmtrC-BS3, SO3domcA-BS3 and SO3dmtrCdomcA consortia produced only 47.67, 50.01 and 28.39 mW/m2 at most, against 452.90 mW/m2 for the intact SO3-BS3 consortium, and they leached 16.7, 18.7 and 13.4 mg/L of total metal ions, 6.13-, 5.48- and 7.64-fold below SO3-BS3.
limitations: The double deletion was indistinguishable from strain BS3 alone.
aspect_assessments.rationale: o30 and o31 are the two read-outs of the SO3 deletion series.
aspect_assessments.scope: The SO3 deletion series in microbial fuel cells and in the anaerobic leaching arm, with BS3 alone as reference.

aspect_assessments.assessment: The cell-free reaction of electrochemically reduced riboflavin with NCM showed absorbance peaks characteristic of oxidised riboflavin growing progressively between 375 and 445 nm over 5-55 min after NCM was added.
limitations: No S. oneidensis cells or cytochromes were present in this reaction.
aspect_assessments.rationale: o32 is the cell-free riboflavin-NCM reaction that is the source of the shuttle mechanism n10.
aspect_assessments.scope: Cell-free reaction at 25 C in the dark.

aspect_assessments.assessment: The claim that riboflavin molecules captured electrons from S. oneidensis cells through MtrC and OmcA and then reduced NCM is supported neither by the consortium-level read-outs of o30 and o31 nor by the cell-free riboflavin reaction of o32. The only observation that names riboflavin is o32, and it shows reduced riboflavin passing electrons to NCM without any S. oneidensis cells or cytochromes present. The authors' own interpretation of the deletion results is that MtrC and OmcA were essential for NCM reduction during metal oxide leaching, and o28 shows that the relative abundance of S. oneidensis on the NCM surface rose with the engineering stage of the consortium.
limitations: No observation in this packet isolates riboflavin from S. oneidensis.
aspect_assessments.rationale: o30 and o31 are the only observations that bear on electron transfer through MtrC and OmcA, and they are read-outs of the deletion series. o32 is a cell-free reaction that shows the shuttle step but does not connect it to S. oneidensis cells.
aspect_assessments.scope: The SO3 deletion series in microbial fuel cells and the cell-free riboflavin-NCM reaction.

aspect_assessments.assessment: The route through MtrC and OmcA and through riboflavin as shuttle is proposed, and the consortium-level observations support the electron-transfer route n05.
limitations: The shuttle step is not isolated from S. oneidensis.
aspect_assessments.rationale: o30 and o31 are the two read-outs of the deletion series, and o28 shows that S. oneidensis colonised the NCM surface with the engineering stage of the consortium.
aspect_assessments.scope: The SO3 deletion series in microbial fuel cells and the anaerobic leaching arm.

findings.description: n13 states that riboflavin molecules captured electrons from S. oneidensis cells through MtrC and OmcA and then reduced NCM, which the visible observations do not show. o30 and o31 are read-outs of the SO3 deletion series and support the electron-transfer route through MtrC and OmcA, while o32 is a cell-free reaction that shows reduced riboflavin passing electrons to NCM without any S. oneidensis cells or cytochromes present. The authors' own interpretation of the deletion results is that MtrC and OmcA were essential for NCM reduction during metal oxide leaching, and o28 shows that the relative abundance of S. oneidensis on the NCM surface rose with the engineering stage of the consortium. The shuttle mechanism n10 and the cell-free riboflavin reaction n17 remain supported at their recorded scope.
The electron-transfer route through MtrC and OmcA and through riboflavin as shuttle is proposed, and the consortium-level observations support it. The route is not isolated from S. oneidensis.

information_requests: Whether the ethanol content of the brewing wastewater was kept constant across the SO3 deletion series.

replace_nodes.statement: Riboflavin is proposed to act as an electron shuttle in the electron-transfer route used by the S. oneidensis-containing consortia, with reduced riboflavin passing electrons to NCM after the electrons have reached the consortium through the outer-membrane c-type cytochromes MtrC and OmcA.

proposed_updates.rationale: The refined wording states the shuttle step of the route that the consortium is presumed to use, without attributing it to riboflavin molecules that captured electrons from S. oneidensis cells through MtrC and OmcA. The evidence remains the consortium-level read-outs of o30 and o31 and the cell-free reaction of o32.

verification_needs.unresolved_question: Are the deletion effects specific to MtrC and OmcA, or are they attributable to the absence of a S. oneidensis partner?
verification_needs.why_informative: The current comparison contrasts the three deletion consortia with the intact SO3-BS3 consortium, so any fall in power density could be attributable to the absence of a S. oneidensis partner rather than to the deletion. needed_observations: riboflavin content of the NCM after each treatment

verification_needs.why_informative: These measurements would directly test whether riboflavin is the shuttle between the consortia and the NCM, rather than the consortium-level read-outs of o30 and o31.

The visible evidence is co-consistent with the authors' mechanism and with a photothermal-only account. Both require Fe-WS2@GOx and NIR: the ROS, MDA and GSH-Px observations in n08 are measured in the same four groups, and the ATP and apoptosis observations in n09 are measured in the same groups. The photothermal account is supported by the temperature rise of 200 ug/mL Fe-WS2 (~29 C) under 808 nm irradiation (o12) and by the TMB assay in which Fe-WS2 generates more ROS with NIR (o11). The two accounts predict different outcomes: the photothermal account predicts that Fe-WS2@GOx+NIR kills bacteria by heating them, which should also kill the same bacteria without Fe-WS2 and without GOx, and that ROS and lipid peroxidation arise from the heat. The authors' mechanism predicts that killing is driven by ROS generated by Fe-WS2 with GOx-derived H2O2 and that the ROS themselves cause lipid peroxidation and the ATP loss. The visible data do not distinguish them. The next step is to test both predictions with matched controls.
